name: Heo Nanseolheon
q: They call the south joy; I see sorrow
Heo Nanseolheon
Crickets outside. My quilt is thin.
Heo Nanseolheon
I moor my oar to watch two ducks fly
Heo Nanseolheon
I pluck a flower. Am I prettier?
Heo Nanseolheon
Now I know: wealth is not what I seek
Heo Nanseolheon
That tree only sees off, never greets
Heo Nanseolheon
I part the red flame to save a moth
Heo Nanseolheon
The lute is done; no one hears it.
Heo Nanseolheon
I laughed at others; now I am here
Heo Nanseolheon
Rise and fall take turns; none escape
Heo Nanseolheon
The bloom fades; the scent never dies
Heo Nanseolheon
I sew brides' gowns and sleep alone
Heo Nanseolheon
Why do owls nest in the phoenix tree?
Heo Nanseolheon
Now I believe it: poetry ruins a man
Heo Nanseolheon
Bones unburied, blood floods the sand
Heo Nanseolheon
Day ends; I lean on my sword and sing
Heo Nanseolheon
Twenty-seven lotus fall on cold frost
Heo Nanseolheon
